transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-30 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Citrine Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Citrine Director of AI), Markus Vogel (Citrine DevOps), Sofia Morales (Finance) - joined briefly

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in: Citrine wants to extend contract 12 months, add reserved capacity for peak shopping events, and onboard EU region with private VPC option. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS requirements, and a short benchmark to validate throughput. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Capacity tiers and burst options
- EU region provisioning and data residency
- Dedicated vs hosted with VPC (tradeoffs)
- Security docs and KMS/HSM integration
- Pricing and contract amendment timeline
- Benchmark plan and sample payloads

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam: Liam here. Priya. Markus.
[00:11] Priya: Hi, thanks Maya.
[00:13] Maya: Cool. Sofia said she'd hop in for the pricing bits later. Ethan and I are on. Ethan, do you want to kick on the technical ask?
[00:21] Ethan: Sure. Hi all. From the notes I have, Citrine wants to bump the reserved capacity by roughly 2x for peak windows and add an EU region with VPC peering. Also the customer asked about a 12-month extension with a blended rate. Is that right, Liam?
[00:37] Liam: Yeah that's the gist. We've grown the checkout ML calls 70% QoQ; the hosted plan is fine day-to-day but during big promos we see latency spikes and cost unpredictability. We're considering Redwood Dedicated for the checkout model and keeping discovery/search on hosted.
[00:52] Maya: That's a common split. Dedicated for the latency-sensitive path, hosted for bursty/less critical. The dedicated pool gives you more predictable p99s, plus pinning a model version is straightforward.
[01:06] Markus: Two operational questions: 1) how fast can the EU region be provisioned? And 2) KMS—do we manage keys or Redwood manages?
[01:15] Ethan: For EU region provisioning, typical lead is 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity activation depending on slot availability; we can prioritize if you sign the amendment sooner. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via your cloud KMS; we can do HSM integrations for Enterprise.
[01:32] Priya: Do you have data residency guarantees? Our legal team requires logs and model inputs not leave EU.
[01:38] Maya: Yes—the EU addendum pins data residency to the EU region for customer data and logs. The control plane will still be managed but the ingestion and KV caches can be kept in-region. We'll include the data residency clause in the amendment.
[01:51] Liam: Cost question—if we reserve capacity and get a lower committed rate, how does that affect burst beyond the reserved pool?
[01:58] Maya: Two options: we can add a burst policy that allows overflow onto the hosted fleet at a blended per-token surcharge, or increase the reserved pool. For brief spikes it’s often cheaper to allow controlled overflow; for prolonged spikes, reserved tier is better.
[02:12] Markus: Overflow is fine as long as the fallback model variant and latency are predictable. We can't have checkout failing.
[02:20] Ethan: We can configure a fallback policy—route to a slightly smaller model variant in the same region to keep p95 under the SLO while shedding cost. We'll show that in the benchmark.
[02:32] Priya: About the benchmark—what's included?
[02:34] Ethan: Proposed: three-day run, 24-hour steady-state with ramp periods, a few 30-minute stress windows to simulate promos. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, token cost, and error rates. We'll also validate KV cache priming for typical session lengths.
[02:50] Liam: That sounds good. We'll provide synthetic payloads and real request distribution.
[02:54] Maya: Great. Sofia, if you're on, we'll share pricing options.
[02:59] Sofia: Yes sorry joined. From finance side, a blended 12-month commitment with a 10% uplift for EU hosting is acceptable as a starting point, but we need the amended quote to include clear unit economics and the overflow surcharge.
[03:15] Maya: We'll put that in the draft. Also we should call out the SLA differences for dedicated pools—lower latency SLOs and a separate uptime SLA.
[03:25] Priya: Security: SOC2 OK, but we need an audit log export format. We also need KMS docs and proof of encryption-in-transit and at-rest.
[03:34] Ethan: We'll share our SOC2 report, ISO paperwork, and a KMS integration guide. For audit logs, we can provide both streaming to your SIEM and periodic export.
[03:43] Markus: Peering—what's the network setup? VPC peering or private link?
[03:48] Ethan: Both supported. For EU on-prem or private deployments we can do private link. For cloud-to-cloud peering we do VPC peering with strict ACLs. We'll send a network diagram.
[03:58] Liam: Timeline: if we sign by Dec 5, when can we realistically be running the benchmark?
[04:03] Maya: If everything is signed and we have your traffic profile, we can schedule the benchmark the week of Dec 6. Provisioning for the dedicated pool in EU would then start and may finish by mid-December, again depending on capacity windows.
[04:15] Priya: Any compliance gating for EU data residency?
[04:18] Ethan: Nothing beyond the addendum and your KMS setup; we'll support the necessary attestations.
[04:23] Liam: On the technical side, one more thing: we're on an older version of the inference client. Will that be a problem?
[04:28] Ethan: We highly recommend the latest SDK; it has streaming and better batching heuristics. But we can run the benchmark with your client to capture realistic numbers, then suggest SDK upgrades for production.
[04:40] Markus: For test harness, I can put up a small cluster to run end-to-end tests, but I need the exact payload format.
[04:45] Ethan: We'll include payload templates and a small Docker test harness.
[04:49] Maya: On pricing, we also will include reserved capacity breakpoints—50%, 100%, 200% of your current committed tokens—and a burst surcharge schedule.
[04:58] Sofia: Good. Also add an exit window clause for the first 90 days in case the latency targets aren't met? Legal will want something like that.
[05:06] Maya: We can propose a remediation SLA and a short-term credit if SLOs aren't met; actual contract language we'll draft with legal.
[05:14] Priya: Competitors—quickly, we've been seeing pitches from OtherCloudAI and EdgeServe. EdgeServe is pushing on on-prem latency claims. What are Redwood differentiators here?
[05:25] Ethan: Practically: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, smart routing between regions and model variants, and built-in KV caching tailored to your session patterns. Also our Optimize toolkit gives concrete quantization/batching recommendations to reduce unit cost.
[05:38] Maya: And ops-wise we provide trace-level dashboards per route and token-level cost breakdowns which helps finance and platform align.
[05:46] Liam: Ok that's helpful.
[05:48] Maya: Anything else?
[05:50] Markus: One more ops ask: can we get a runbook for failover—if EU region goes down, how does traffic failover to US without leaking EU data?
[05:58] Ethan: We'll create a failover playbook: routing policies that keep EU-customer data in EU where possible; if forced to route out, we'd use anonymization and only route inference to a vetted backup model that strips PII. We'll document triggers and RTO/RPO.
[06:12] Liam: Sounds good.
[06:13] Maya: All right, recap: Redwood sends amended quote and contract amendment; Redwood to share SOC2, ISO, KMS guide and network diagram; SE to prepare benchmark plan and test harness; Citrine to share traffic profile and pick a benchmark week.
[06:30] Priya: We'll target the week of Dec 6 for benchmark.
[06:33] Sofia: Finance will review draft quote and revert by Dec 4.
[06:36] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark prep and attach the documents.
[06:44] Liam: Thanks all.
[06:46] Meeting end.
